Mimosa Posts Steady Output in Latest Results, Cites Stable Market Conditions

Mimosa, a key player in Zimbabwe’s Metals & Mining sector, has reported steady quarterly results, maintaining its track record of consistent output in the face of fluctuating global commodity prices. The company, which primarily operates in the Midlands province, announced a total production of 31,500 ounces of platinum group metals for the quarter ending March 2024, in line with its performance over the previous year.

According to Managing Director Tendai Moyo, the company’s operations have benefited from “stable market conditions and continued focus on operational efficiency.” Moyo added, “We are pleased with the resilience shown by our team and the reliability of our supply chain partners. Our commitment to safety and community engagement remains a pillar of our strategy.”

Industry analysts welcomed the results, noting that Mimosa has weathered broader sector challenges, including volatile metal prices and rising operational costs. “Mimosa’s discipline in cost management and ongoing investment in local infrastructure have underpinned their steady performance,” said Tapiwa Chirwa, a mining analyst at Harare-based consultancy Mineral Insights.

The Zimbabwe Chamber of Mines also acknowledged Mimosa’s role in supporting local employment and development initiatives. “Their consistent output provides vital foreign exchange and helps sustain livelihoods in the region,” said Chamber spokesperson Rudo Dube.

Looking ahead, company officials expressed cautious optimism. “We continue to monitor market trends and invest in sustainable practices,” Moyo said. No major operational changes or disruptions have been reported, and Mimosa confirmed that all production and export activities are proceeding as normal.
